s1.title: RASIN Integrated Security Center
why.label: Light up your knowledge
why.a2: Because security starts from a foundation that never shakes
why.note: In Arabic, rasuna means to become firm and well set; rasin describes what is steady and does not waver, as in a solid building. We took our project's name from that meaning, so that saying it is itself a promise of steadiness: protection that stands firm, and trust that never wavers.
s1.tagline: A fortress of stone, guarding a treasure of data.
s2.lead: A hypothetical center specializing in cybersecurity and information protection.
s2.why: RASIN is a fictional organization born of imagination: a center for information security and digital protection, built around the course subject: information security. It draws on the Internet of Things (IoT) for the idea of connected devices that detect and alert, and works to protect data and counter digital cyberattacks. Because RASIN's most precious holdings are data no one can see, the project tells how we guard that digital treasure with tools you can touch: a fence and a gate, a camera that never blinks, and a door that opens only for those authorized to enter. Information is protected in the building before it is protected on the network.
s3.explain: Sensitivity rises with height: the higher a person goes, the more verification points they pass through.
cia.c.def: Ensuring that only authorized people can access information.
cia.i.def: Protecting information from unauthorized modification or destruction.
cia.a.def: Ensuring that authorized people can reach information and systems whenever they need them.
cia.c.1: Visitors are kept south of the turnstile line.
cia.c.2: All lifts and stairs sit behind that line.
cia.c.3: The executive meeting room faces the lift, so visitors never see the offices.
cia.c.4: Opaque glazing on the operations-center façade.
cia.i.1: The server room and archive sit behind a mantrap with two-factor verification.
cia.i.2: A single logged point for receiving records.
cia.a.1: A “protected vertical spine”: dry rooms on the ground floor, the server room on the first, the archive on the second — no water pipes.
cia.a.2: An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) room and a backup generator.
s3.title: Security Framework Supporting the CIA Triad
st.title: Security Strategies & Controls in RASIN
st.did.p: Multiple, integrated layers of protection from the outer perimeter to the high-security zones, so bypassing one control does not breach the whole system. It is the starting point: everything below is a layer within it.
st.did.a: The five security zones shown above, from the perimeter (Z0) to high security (Z4); each zone is a separate layer with a stricter check than the one before, so passing one layer does not open the next.
st.phys.p: Protecting the facility and its assets from unauthorized entry, tampering, or unlawful access to sensitive devices and information.
st.phys.a: Six integrated systems: physical barriers, surveillance, unauthorized-access detection, guarding and screening, access control, and environmental controls.
st.ac.p: Regulating access to zones and resources according to approved permission levels, limiting unauthorized access.
st.ac.a: An access matrix for nine job roles and a verification requirement for every zone. Access follows the role, not just the floor: senior management cannot enter the server room or archive by virtue of their position.
st.comp.p: The means that enforce the access decision at each point: they verify the person, log the entry, and prevent tailgating.
st.comp.a: 40 control points spread across the security zones; their types, locations and how the mantrap works are detailed in the Access Control card.
st.iam.p: Tying access to a person's identity, job role and clearance level, and managing and reviewing those permissions.
st.iam.a: At the physical-access level: staff cards are tied to the role matrix, Z4 keeps an entry/exit log, and the list of two-factor holders is reviewed monthly. The model does not include a digital IAM system for system accounts.
st.enc.p: Turning information into a form unreadable to unauthorized parties, protecting its confidentiality in storage or in transit.
st.enc.a: Documented scope: laptops that leave the building are encrypted (ISO 7.9). The model does not document encryption for data in transit or for other systems, so it is not claimed.
fn.deter.d: Discouraging an attempt in the first place by showing the site is protected: a fence, visible cameras and guards.
fn.detect.d: Spotting an attempt as it happens and raising the alarm, through sensors and cameras.
fn.delay.d: Slowing an intruder with successive barriers and doors, buying the security team time to arrive before the target is reached.
fn.respond.d: Acting to stop the incident and limit its impact: guards, an alert to the control room, or automatic fire suppression.
fn.off: This system does not perform this function.
s4.c1.title: Physical barriers
s4.c1.w1: A 2.4 m anti-climb fence fitted with a vibration sensor.
s4.c1.w2: Two gates: one for pedestrians, one for vehicles with a hydraulic road blocker.
s4.c1.w3: Fixed bollards in front of the entrance.
s4.c1.w4: Laminated security glass, and bars on the rear ground-floor windows.
s4.c1.where: Along the whole site perimeter (280 m), at both gates, across the entrance forecourt, and on the building façades.
s4.c1.why: The road blocker holds a vehicle until it has been inspected and stops a vehicle-ramming attempt; the vibration cable pinpoints the section being climbed or cut, so the PTZ camera turns to it.
s4.c2.title: Surveillance
s4.c2.w2: Every Z4 room has 80% coverage or more; the server room and archive 100%, the operations center 99%.
s4.c2.where: PTZ cameras on the fence corners, a licence-plate camera at the vehicle gate, a camera facing the turnstiles, and two opposing cameras in the server room and in the archive.
s4.c2.why: Continuous monitoring and recorded evidence of every event; visible cameras deter before they detect. Operations-center cameras capture movement and people, not screen content.
s4.c3.title: Unauthorized-access detection
s4.c3.w1: 24 sensors and alarm buttons: motion detectors, door contacts, glass-break detectors and silent panic buttons.
s4.c3.where: Along the whole fence, ground-floor windows, emergency exits, and the server room and archive; panic buttons at reception, the guard post and the control room.
s4.c3.why: Motion detectors catch any movement outside working hours or without a logged entry; a panic button sends a silent alarm to the control room without the threat noticing.
s4.c4.title: Guarding & screening
s4.c4.w1: 8 guard posts, with a required force of about 34 guards.
s4.c4.w2: A nine-step visitor procedure, and four verification layers before the lobby.
s4.c4.where: Both gate kiosks on the site, staffed around the clock; the entrance, screening and control-room posts on the ground floor; and a mobile patrol around the building and perimeter.
s4.c4.why: The human element verifies, decides and responds where devices are not enough. The four entrance layers: face camera, then the vestibule under the guard's eye, then ID, X-ray and metal detector, then the badge.
s4.c5.title: Access control
s4.c5.w1: 40 points: card readers, two-factor readers, turnstiles and mantraps.
s4.c5.where: Turnstiles on the ground floor, a card reader on every department door, and a mantrap with two two-factor readers in front of the server room and archive.
s4.c5.why: A stolen card alone cannot open a Z4 zone, and the mantrap's second door will not open until the first has closed, so two people cannot enter on one card.
s4.c6.title: Environmental factors
s4.c6.w2: Perimeter and emergency lighting; ventilation with protected air intakes on the roof.
s4.c6.w3: Dual precision cooling (N+1), a generator and an uninterruptible power supply.
s4.c6.w4: Clean-agent gas suppression and water-leak detection.
s4.c6.where: The server, power and archive rooms; the backup generator in the service yard; air intakes on the roof; lighting on the fence, forecourt and car parks.
s4.c6.why: Clean-agent gas puts out a fire without water, so servers and paper are not damaged. Lighting deters and keeps the cameras effective at night.
s5.ecc.name: Essential Cybersecurity Controls
s5.ecc.scope: National Cybersecurity Authority · Subdomain 2-14 Physical Security
s5.iso.name: Annex A — Physical controls
s5.nist.name: Physical and Environmental Protection family (PE)
ecc.1.a: Every device is linked to its requirement (R-3 to R-11).
ecc.2.a: Fence and barriers, unauthorized-access sensors, guarding.
ecc.3: Scope: access, monitoring, records, disposal, equipment.
ecc.3.a: Two-factor readers and mantraps, cameras, media vault, destruction room, environmental protection.
ecc.4.a: Every six months and after any incident.
iso.1.a: The fence and its vibration sensor, both gates, bollards, the road blocker, windows and façades, and perimeter lighting.
iso.2.a: Gate 1, the vestibule and turnstiles, card readers, the licence-plate camera, the metal detector, the X-ray machine and guard posts.
iso.3.a: Steel doors for Z4 zones, two-factor readers, mantraps, and windows and façades.
iso.4.a: Fixed and PTZ cameras; motion, door and glass-break detectors; panic buttons; perimeter lighting; and central monitoring (BMS).
iso.5: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
iso.5.a: Temperature, humidity and water-leak sensors, early smoke detection, clean-agent suppression, ventilation and central monitoring.
iso.6.a: No unescorted visitors in Z4, and a clean-desk policy.
iso.7.a: No documents left on desks after hours, automatic screen lock, and a locked cabinet in every office.
iso.8.a: Precision cooling for technical rooms, and servers in locked racks.
iso.9.a: Laptops are encrypted and logged out and back in through the staff entrance.
iso.10.a: Backups kept in fire-resistant safes in the media vault, with every removal and return logged at the receiving point.
iso.11.a: The backup generator and UPS, precision cooling, ventilation, and the emergency power-off switch.
iso.12.a: Cables run in closed conduits; network ports are disabled in Z1 and Z2.
iso.13.a: Maintenance technicians are escorted inside Z4 zones, and tools are inventoried on entry and exit.
iso.14: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
iso.14.a: Paper and media are destroyed in the destruction room before leaving, under camera, with a signed destruction record.
pe.3.a: Card and two-factor readers, turnstiles, mantraps, guard posts, the road blocker, and windows and façades.
pe.6.a: Fixed, PTZ and licence-plate cameras, unauthorized-access sensors and panic buttons.
pe.10.a: An emergency power-off switch by the door, with a cover against accidental presses.
pe.11.a: An auto-start backup generator, and a UPS covering servers, the operations center and security systems until the generator runs.
pe.12.a: Battery lighting for corridors and stairs, and illuminated exit signs.
pe.13.a: Smoke detectors, early smoke detection (VESDA), and clean-agent suppression in the server, power and archive rooms.
pe.14.a: Temperature and humidity sensors, precision cooling (N+1), and general ventilation and air-conditioning.
pe.15.a: No water pipes above technical rooms or the archive; leak-detection cables under the server floor and on the archive ceiling.
pe.16.a: An X-ray machine for bags and parcels.
ch.title: Can you reach the server room?
ch.lead: Play the intruder: choose your method at each layer and see which RASIN control stops you.
ch.next: Suppose you got past it: next layer
ch.endTitle: You did not reach the server room
ch.endText: RASIN stopped you at each of the five layers, and even when we assumed you got past one, the next was waiting. That is defense in depth: protection never rests on a single control.
ch.s1.q: The site fence is in front of you. How will you get in?
ch.s1.o1.w: A cable along the whole fence pinpoints the section being climbed or cut, and the PTZ camera turns to it.
ch.s1.o2: Ram the vehicle gate with a car
ch.s1.o2.w: It holds a vehicle until it has been inspected and stops a ramming attempt, and fixed bollards guard the entrance.
ch.s1.o3: Walk in through the pedestrian gate as a visitor
ch.s1.o3.c: The guard booth at the gate
ch.s1.o3.w: Both gate booths are staffed around the clock, and a visitor reaches the building only through registration and screening.
ch.s2.q: You are at the building door. What will you do?
ch.s2.o1: Walk in with a phone and a memory stick in my bag
ch.s2.o1.w: A metal-detector gate and an X-ray scanner check every bag, and phones and storage media are left in the visitor lockers before entry.
ch.s2.o2.w: Two doors in a row stop anyone rushing straight in, in full view of the entrance guard.
ch.s2.o3.w: It detects entry attempts through ground-floor windows, and the rear windows have bars and laminated glass.
ch.s3.q: You are in the lobby and the offices are behind the turnstiles. How will you cross?
ch.s3.o1.c: The turnstile camera and the control room
ch.s3.o1.w: A camera facing the turnstiles records every crossing, and the guard and control room watches the cameras around the clock.
ch.s3.o2: Slip inside from the meeting room
ch.s3.o2.w: Everything a visitor needs is south of the turnstile line, and the visitor corridor does not connect to the staff corridor at all.
ch.s3.o3.c: The service entrance and escorted technicians
ch.s3.o3.w: Technicians and deliveries come through the service entrance where parcels are checked, and no technician works in a Z4 zone without an escort and a tool check on the way in and out.
ch.s4.q: You are in the inner corridor and the server room is on the first floor. How will you go up?
ch.s4.o1.w: The lifts work only with a card, and the lift stops on the first floor only for those cleared for it.
ch.s4.o2.w: Leaving the stairwell is free, but getting back onto any floor needs a card.
ch.s4.o3: Hide in the building until everyone leaves
ch.s4.o3.w: It catches any movement outside working hours or without a logged entry.
ch.s5.q: You are at the mantrap in front of the server room. Your last attempt?
ch.s5.o1.w: Entry needs a card plus a PIN or fingerprint, so a stolen card alone does not open the door.
ch.s5.o2.w: Its two doors never open together and the second will not open until the first has closed, so two people cannot enter on one card.
ch.s5.o3: Try at night after everyone has left
ch.s5.o3.w: The server room has 100% camera coverage, and the motion detector catches any movement outside working hours or without a logged entry.
gl.mantrap.d: A small space between two doors that never open together, so only one person gets through at a time.
gl.ups.d: Batteries that keep critical equipment running the moment power fails, until the generator starts.
gl.n1.d: One spare unit ready to take over at once if any main unit fails.
gl.vesda.d: A system that keeps sampling the air to detect smoke before any flame appears.
gl.ecc.d: The minimum cybersecurity controls issued by Saudi Arabia's National Cybersecurity Authority.
gl.bms.d: A central platform that monitors the building's systems and gathers their alarms in one place.
gl.bollard.d: Fixed, impact-resistant posts that stop vehicles from ramming the entrance.
gl.gas.d: A gas that puts out fire without water and leaves no residue to damage equipment or paper.
gl.2fa.d: Proving identity with two factors together: a card plus a PIN or fingerprint.

s7.m1: Security is built before it is programmed.
s7.m1s: In RASIN, the plan drew the boundaries of protection before any system came online; every wall, corridor and door is a security decision.
s7.m2: Every piece of information is a trust; every device is a responsibility.
s7.m2s: Data protection is not limited to digital systems; every asset carries value worth protecting.
s7.m3: Physical and information security are one system.
s7.m3s: Protection is never complete with a secure wall or an advanced digital system alone, but with the integration of architectural design and cybersecurity.
nca.badge: Based on the National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA)
s7.nogap.t2: When Security Starts with a Decision
s7.nogap.leadA: does not begin when an attack happens, but long before it — in the
s7.nogap.leadB: built by small decisions we make every day without noticing their weight.
s7.nogap.d1s: An unknown link or an urgent message can be a door left ajar; checking the source closes it before anyone knocks.
s7.nogap.d2s: A strong password, sharing only what is needed, and a device never left unlocked for passers-by.
s7.nogap.d3s: Security policies are not restrictions; they are a shared agreement that none of us will be the weakest link.
s7.nogap.riskB: , risk is the product of a threat's likelihood and its impact. Security awareness is a proactive line of defense that works on both: it lowers the likelihood of a threat succeeding and limits its impact if it does — making
s7.nogap.riskC: a result rather than luck, and preserving the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information.
s7.nogap.btnNote: Awareness booklet issued by the National Cybersecurity Authority
s7.nogap.quote: “Give danger no chance, and leave risk no opening; protecting information begins with awareness and continues with action.”
s7.nogap.note: Note: “La Tiftah Majal” (Leave No Opening) is an awareness campaign launched by Saudi Arabia's National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA); this section links its message to the information-security and risk-management concepts of the RASIN project.

s8.link: Defending the homeland reaches beyond its visible borders, into a digital space where secrets are kept, assets are walled with protection, and truth is guarded from being tainted by rumour or twisted by hearsay. Every piece of information protected, every rumour contained, and every word checked for truth is a front of defense. Let us make our digital responsibility a national pledge and our awareness a shield; homelands are protected not only by heroes in the field, but also by the awareness of their people in every space.
